name: frontend-common
description: Framework-independent frontend skills: debugging, codebase exploration, and knowledge lookup that apply the same way on React, Next, Angular, Vue, or plain JS. Also holds the gate for framework-specific upstream skills (Vercel/TanStack/etc.) — detects which frontend framework(s) a project actually uses and confirms with the engineer before recommending or installing any framework-specific bundle, so a React project never ends up with Angular skills loaded and vice versa. Three further skills (fe-eslint-setup, fe-prettier-setup, fe-test-setup) use the same detect-then-confirm pattern to scaffold tooling — each runs the framework's own first-party setup command (next lint, ng add @angular-eslint/schematics, npx sv add, npm init @eslint/config, npm init playwright, …) rather than hand-writing configs or guessing package names.
_schema_note: Verified against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/manifest-reference (checked 2026-10-09). The 'skills' array is intentionally omitted: it only adds to the default skills/ scan and every skill here already lives under skills/, so listing it was redundant. 'owners' moved under 'metadata' — it isn't a recognized top-level field and would otherwise be silently stripped with a validate warning; 'metadata' is the documented place for free-form data Claude Code doesn't read.
